title: When the World Got Connected
question: How did voyages by sea tie the whole world together?
hook: Ships sent to find trade routes ended up linking continents that had never been in touch.
idea: Overseas exploration connected previously isolated parts of the world into a world-system and laid the groundwork for globalization.

beats.prompt: Ships now cross between the Old World and the New for the first time. Besides gold and spices, what also travels between the hemispheres?

choices.label: Only precious metals, which are the one thing worth shipping
choices.feedback: Tempting, but the transfer included far more than goods of high value.

choices.label: Plants, animals, people, communicable diseases and culture
Nothing else, since the oceans keep living things apart
choices.feedback: The voyages carried plants, animals and diseases right across the oceans.

beats.explain: European exploration started the Columbian exchange: the transfer of plants, animals, human populations, communicable diseases and culture across the hemispheres.

items: Portuguese begin systematic exploring of Africa's Atlantic coast
Bartolomeu Dias reaches the Indian Ocean
Spain funds Columbus to sail west across the Atlantic
Vasco da Gama reaches India by sailing around Africa
beats.explain: The Portuguese began in 1418, Dias reached the Indian Ocean in 1488, Columbus was funded in 1492, and da Gama reached India in 1498.

beats.prompt: Match each voyage or route to what it did.
pairs: Established a sea route to India in 1498
Marked the beginning of colonization in the Americas
Opened a route from the Atlantic to the Pacific
Linked the Americas and Asia across the Pacific
beats.explain: Together these voyages joined Europe, Asia and the Americas by sea.

beats.prompt: Sort each undertaking by the crown behind it.
items: Voyages along the West African coast
Expeditions to the Azores and Madeira
beats.explain: Portuguese exploration moved from nearby islands down Africa's coast to India, while Spain's major early undertakings reached across the Atlantic and Pacific.
